title: Microsoft Edge: auto-open Copilot side pane for links opened from Outlook
summary: Hold: the briefing implies that DLP controls whether the pane appears, although Microsoft documents only that DLP prevents access to protected page content. It also describes profile-scoped browser policies as tenant-wide controls and expands eligible links to every same-tenant email link. The policy names, Group Policy paths and registry settings are supported.

claims.quote: When users open links from Outlook, Microsoft Edge can automatically open the Copilot side pane

claims.quote: This policy doesn't control access for Copilot with enterprise data protection (EDP). Access for Copilot with EDP is controlled by the EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft's policy page does not define which links are eligible.
claims.quote: Searched: "M365LinksAutoOpenCopilotEnabled" eligible links email context control suggestion chips approval. Read the auto-open policy reference and Intune's June 8, 2026 update; neither defines eligibility beyond same-tenant Outlook web links.

claims.claim: The auto-open policy page documents no separate control over how much of the originating email is used.
claims.quote: Searched: "M365LinksAutoOpenCopilotEnabled" "email" "context" control. Read the auto-open policy reference in full; it describes email context but no email-content selection or amount setting.

claims.claim: The auto-open policy page does not describe external-sender links as covered.
claims.quote: Searched: "M365LinksAutoOpenCopilotEnabled" eligible links email context control suggestion chips approval. Read the auto-open policy reference and Intune's June 8, 2026 update; both describe emails sent from the same tenant.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described what this feature's suggestion chips can do without user approval.
claims.quote: Searched: "M365LinksAutoOpenCopilotEnabled" "suggestion" "approval". Read the auto-open policy reference and roadmap; no approval mechanism is specified. Results about Cowork approvals and browsing with Copilot describe different features.

claims.claim: The auto-open policy page names no licence, meter or charge for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "M365LinksAutoOpenCopilotEnabled" licensing license pricing meter Copilot Outlook side pane. Read the policy reference in full, Copilot requirements and licensing search excerpts; no auto-open-specific licence, meter or charge was stated.

claims.claim: The roadmap record names no licence, meter or charge.
claims.quote: Admins can control availability to this feature using the M365LinksAutoOpenCopilotEnabled policy.

claims.claim: The policy pages do not explicitly state whether unconfigured EU profiles get the automatically opening pane.
claims.quote: Searched: "M365LinksAutoOpenCopilotEnabled" "EU" unconfigured automatic open. Read all three policy references; EU page-access defaults and explicitly disabled policies are described, but the auto-open outcome for unconfigured EU profiles is not stated.

claims.claim: The new pane appears next to every same-tenant email link a user opens in Edge.
claims.quote: This policy controls whether Microsoft Edge automatically opens the Microsoft Copilot side pane when users open eligible web links from Outlook emails sent from the same tenant.
claims.fix: Replace "next to every same-tenant email link a user opens in Edge" with "when a user opens an eligible web link from an Outlook email sent from the same tenant". The policy does not promise coverage of every link.

claims.claim: DLP decisions determine whether users see the automatically opening pane.
claims.quote: Searched: "M365LinksAutoOpenCopilotEnabled" DLP protected pages automatic pane visibility. Read all three policy references and Purview DLP excerpts; DLP blocks page-content access, but none states that it suppresses this pane's automatic opening.
claims.fix: Replace "so existing page-context and DLP decisions now also decide whether users see this pane" with "so disabling either page-context policy also disables the auto-open feature. DLP-protected page content remains inaccessible to Copilot."

claims.claim: The auto-open Group Policy and registry control has tenant scope.
claims.quote: Searched: "M365LinksAutoOpenCopilotEnabled" tenant policy per profile scope. Read the policy reference: "Per Profile: Yes". The documented Group Policy and registry setting does not state tenant-wide enforcement.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].scope to "user" and replace the rendered "Tenant" label with "User". Append to its note: "Applies per Edge profile." The reference documents profile-scoped application, not a tenant-wide switch.

claims.claim: The EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext Group Policy and registry control has tenant scope.
claims.quote: Searched: "M365LinksAutoOpenCopilotEnabled" tenant policy per profile scope. Read EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext: "Per Profile: Yes"; it applies only to Entra-account users in Edge's side pane. No tenant-wide enforcement is stated.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].scope to "user" and replace the rendered "Tenant" label with "User". Append to its note: "Applies per Edge profile."

claims.claim: The CopilotPageContext Group Policy and registry control has tenant scope.
claims.quote: Searched: "M365LinksAutoOpenCopilotEnabled" tenant policy per profile scope. Read CopilotPageContext: "Per Profile: Yes" and "This policy applies only to Microsoft Entra ID profiles in Microsoft Edge." No tenant-wide enforcement is stated.
claims.fix: Set controls[2].scope to "user" and replace the rendered "Tenant" label with "User". Append to its note: "Applies per Edge profile."

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to review DLP policies, but the controls table has no DLP-policy row.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Review which pages your DLP policies protect". The three control rows are M365LinksAutoOpenCopilotEnabled, EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext and CopilotPageContext.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet "Review which pages your DLP policies protect, since Copilot can't read those pages." Keep the supported DLP restriction in Risk assessment; do not add an unverified control row.
